about: Advanced Automation (AAU), FH Technikum Wien master's programme, summer term 2021: the 28 Rechenbeispiele of Kubinger (2021a) and the three MATLAB lab tasks (Kubinger 2021b; Kubinger and Lang 2021), animated step by step, each step with the MATLAB that gives its result. Equations from the slides of Kubinger (2021), cited by PDF page as 'slides p. N' (docs/sources/slide-conventions.md); solution-sheet values from the handwritten sheets S1, S2 and M, cited by file and page (docs/sources/solution-sheets.md). tests/unit/labs-data.test.js recomputes every practice answer with the core.

labs.title: From equations to A, b, cᵀ, d
labs.idea: Each state equation is one row of A and b, each output equation one row of cᵀ and d: watch every coefficient go to its cell, then run the model.
labs.lecture: Kubinger (2021a), Beispiele 1–3, pp. 2–4; Kubinger (2021), slides pp. 3–4
labs.law: ẋ = A x + b u,  v = cᵀx + d u
labs.lawTex: \dot{x} = A x + b u, \quad v = c^T x + d u

equations.eq: ẋ = A x + b u, v = cᵀx + d u
equations.tex: \dot{x} = A x + b u, \quad v = c^T x + d u
equations.note: SISO state space: A n × n, b n × 1, cᵀ 1 × n, d a scalar

equations.eq: ẋ = A x + B u, v = C x + D u
equations.tex: \dot{x} = A x + B u, \quad v = C x + D u
equations.note: Two inputs or outputs (System C, System 4): B, C and D become matrices

practice.question: System B (Beispiel 1): what is a23, the entry of A for x3 in the equation of ẋ2?
System 3 (Beispiel 2): what is d?
practice.solution: v = 3x1 − 2x2 + 2x3 + 3u: the input goes straight through with factor 3.

practice.question: System C (Beispiel 1): what is D's entry for u2 in v1?
practice.solution: v1 = x1 − x2 + x3 + 2u1 − u2: row 1 of D is [2 −1].

labs.title: G(s), RNF and BNF
labs.idea: The same system in other states: its transfer function's coefficients fill the RNF's last row or the BNF's last column, and the step response does not change.

equations.note: Transfer function from the state space; E is the identity
Regelungsnormalform: ones above the diagonal, −a_i in the last row

equations.tex: A_{BNF} = A_{RNF}^T,\; b_{BNF} = \begin{bmatrix} b_0 \\ \vdots \\ b_{n-1} \end{bmatrix},\; c^T_{BNF} = [0 \cdots 1]
equations.note: Beobachtungsnormalform: ones below the diagonal, −a_i in the last column

equations.eq: stable ⇔ every root of det(sE − A) = 0 has Re < 0
equations.note: Poles from the characteristic equation

practice.solution: b0, the numerator's constant term of s² + 2s + 3.

labs.title: Controllable, observable, stable?
labs.idea: b and Ab span a parallelogram whose area is det Q_S: zero area, and some direction can never be steered. cᵀ and cᵀA do the same for what the output can see.
labs.law: Q_S = [b  Ab  …  Aⁿ⁻¹b],  Q_B = [cᵀ; cᵀA; …; cᵀAⁿ⁻¹]
labs.lawTex: Q_S = [b \; Ab \; \cdots \; A^{n-1}b], \quad Q_B = \begin{bmatrix} c^T \\ c^T A \\ \vdots \\ c^T A^{n-1} \end{bmatrix}

equations.eq: Q_S = [b Ab … Aⁿ⁻¹b]; controllable ⇔ det Q_S ≠ 0
equations.note: Steuerbarkeitsmatrix; or rank Q_S = n
Beobachtbarkeitsmatrix; or rank Q_B = n

equations.eq: det(sE − A) = 0, stable ⇔ all Re λi < 0
equations.note: Stable, marginally stable (simple poles on the axis) or unstable

labs.title: Pole placement and the prefilter
labs.idea: In the RNF each coefficient of the closed loop is a_i + r_(i+1): set it to the wanted p_i. Then carry rᵀ back to the plant's states and scale the reference with Kf.

equations.eq: u = −rᵀx + K_F·w, ẋ = (A − b rᵀ)x + b K_F w
equations.tex: u = -r^T x + K_F w, \quad \dot{x} = (A - b r^T) x + b K_F w
equations.note: State controller with prefilter

equations.eq: det(sE − (A − b rᵀ)) = sⁿ + p(n−1)sⁿ⁻¹ + … + p0
equations.note: The wanted characteristic polynomial from the wanted poles
Coefficient comparison in the RNF

equations.eq: x_RNF = S x, S = Q_S,RNF·Q_S⁻¹, rᵀ = rᵀ_RNF·S
equations.tex: x_{RNF} = S x,\; S = Q_{S,RNF} Q_S^{-1},\; r^T = r^T_{RNF} S
equations.note: Back to the plant's states (the transform is on slides p. 5; S worked here from Q_S,RNF = S·Q_S)
Prefilter: the steady output follows w

labs.title: The Luenberger observer
labs.idea: A copy of the plant, corrected by ℓ times the output error: in the BNF its gain is p_i − a_i, and the estimate closes in on the true state at the pace of the observer poles.

equations.eq: dx̂/dt = A x̂ + b u + ℓ(v − cᵀx̂)
equations.note: The observer: the plant's model plus a correction
The error dies away when A − ℓcᵀ is stable
Coefficient comparison in the BNF
Back to the plant's states (worked here from Q_B,BNF = Q_B·S⁻¹)

Beispiel 18: the second entry of ℓ for s = −3, −4?
practice.solution: Already a BNF with a0 = 3, a1 = −6; s² + 7s + 12: ℓ2 = 7 + 6 = 13.

practice.question: Beispiel 18: the first entry of ℓ?

labs.title: Controller and observer together
labs.idea: Design the controller first, then the observer, faster: the loop of order 2n has both sets of poles side by side, and a wrong first estimate fades out.
labs.law: [ẋ; dx̂/dt] = [A  −b rᵀ; ℓcᵀ  A − b rᵀ − ℓcᵀ][x; x̂] + [b; b] K_F w
labs.lawTex: \begin{bmatrix} \dot{x} \\ \dot{\hat{x}} \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} A & -b r^T \\ \ell c^T & A - b r^T - \ell c^T \end{bmatrix} \begin{bmatrix} x \\ \hat{x} \end{bmatrix} + \begin{bmatrix} b \\ b \end{bmatrix} K_F w

equations.eq: [ẋ; dx̂/dt] = [A −b rᵀ; ℓcᵀ A − b rᵀ − ℓcᵀ][x; x̂] + [b; b]K_F w
equations.tex: \begin{bmatrix} \dot{x} \\ \dot{\hat{x}} \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} A & -b r^T \\ \ell c^T & A - b r^T - \ell c^T \end{bmatrix} \begin{bmatrix} x \\ \hat{x} \end{bmatrix} + \begin{bmatrix} b \\ b \end{bmatrix} K_F w
equations.note: The loop with observer, order 2n

equations.eq: eig = eig(A − b rᵀ) ∪ eig(A − ℓcᵀ)
equations.note: Separation theorem

labs.title: Linearisation by the tangent
labs.idea: Near the working point a curve is its tangent: sin y becomes y, cos y becomes 1, and every entry of A, b, cᵀ, d is one slope at x0 = 0.

equations.note: Tangent method
Relative error of the tangent
Beispiel 23 linearised at y0 = 0

equations.tex: a_{ij} = \frac{\partial f_i}{\partial x_j}, \; b_i = \frac{\partial f_i}{\partial u}
equations.note: Each entry the slope of one term (the slides give the one-variable tangent only)

practice.question: Beispiel 25: a21?

practice.question: Beispiel 25: a22 (the tan term)?

labs.title: A circuit in state space
labs.idea: One state per energy store: the coil's current and the capacitor's voltage. Kirchhoff's mesh rule gives the rows of A; only Uh leaves the housing.
labs.law: L1·diL/dt = Us − (R1 + R2)iL − uC,  C2·duC/dt = iL
labs.lawTex: L_1 \frac{di_L}{dt} = U_s - (R_1 + R_2) i_L - u_C, \quad C_2 \frac{du_C}{dt} = i_L

equations.note: x = [iL; uC], u = Us, v = Uh
Both non-zero: controllable and observable

Beispiel 20: det Q_B, in Ω/s?

labs.title: The DC motor
labs.idea: The armature mesh and the torque balance give two states, current and speed; the load torque enters as a disturbance through its own column.
labs.law: UA = RA·iA + LA·diA/dt + c·2π·n,  J·2π·dn/dt = c·iA − ML
labs.lawTex: U_A = R_A i_A + L_A \frac{di_A}{dt} + c\,2\pi n, \quad J\,2\pi \frac{dn}{dt} = c\, i_A - M_L

equations.eq: UA = RA iA + LA diA/dt + c·2π·n; J·2π·dn/dt = c·iA − ML
equations.tex: U_A = R_A i_A + L_A \dot{i}_A + c\,2\pi n, \; J\,2\pi\,\dot{n} = c\, i_A - M_L
equations.note: Armature mesh and torque balance, friction neglected

equations.tex: A = \begin{bmatrix} -\frac{R_A}{L_A} & -\frac{2\pi c}{L_A} \\ \frac{c}{2\pi J} & 0 \end{bmatrix},\; b = \begin{bmatrix} \frac{1}{L_A} \\ 0 \end{bmatrix},\; b_z = \begin{bmatrix} 0 \\ -\frac{1}{2\pi J} \end{bmatrix}
equations.note: x = [iA; n]; b_z worked here from the torque balance

labs.title: The crane trolley, linearised
labs.idea: The load swings under the trolley: a nonlinear pair of equations that, for small swings, becomes four linear states, angle, angular speed, position and speed.

equations.note: The swing

equations.eq: v̇ = [Fa + mL g sin φ cos φ + mL l ω² sin φ]/(mK + mL sin² φ)
equations.note: The trolley, by Lagrange (worked here; M, p. 53 writes −mL ω² l sin φ)

equations.tex: A = \begin{bmatrix} 0 & 1 & 0 & 0 \\ -\frac{g(m_K + m_L)}{m_K l} & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 1 \\ \frac{m_L g}{m_K} & 0 & 0 & 0 \end{bmatrix},\; b = \begin{bmatrix} 0 \\ -\frac{1}{m_K l} \\ 0 \\ \frac{1}{m_K} \end{bmatrix}
equations.note: x = [φ; ω; x; v], at φ = 0

labs.title: Lab task 0: six controllers compared
labs.idea: One plant, six pole choices: slow, fast, swinging, LQ, Butterworth and your own. Their step responses show what each choice buys in rise time, overshoot and settling.
labs.lecture: Kubinger (2021b), task 0, pp. 1–2; Kubinger (2021), slides pp. 14–18, 31–32

equations.eq: J = ∫(xᵀQx + uᵀRu) dt → min, rᵀ = R⁻¹bᵀS
equations.tex: J = \int_0^\infty (x^T Q x + u^T R u)\,dt, \quad r^T = R^{-1} b^T S
equations.note: LQ controller; here Q = λ·c cᵀ, R = 1
